extracted.intended_audience: public relations educators, students, and practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing and managing press releases and related public relations writing within a broader public relations management framework; includes managerial considerations, writing objectives, timing, distribution, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations education as social science
rubrics_metrics.description: Be taught as a social science with both an academic and a professional emphasis; drawn from both professional practice and scholarly theory; help public relations to become more analytical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The IPRA-recommended approach: integrate social science knowledge into PR education so practitioners can analyze problems and apply theory to practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate theory and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a comprehensive conceptual framework—drawn from systems theory—that demonstrates what public relations does for an organization and how that contribution can be measured and evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use social science theories to explain common PR problems and to plan, coordinate, and evaluate PR programs; trace ideas to original research where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-way symmetric model preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor the two-way symmetric model of public relations — a model based on negotiation, compromise, and understanding — over the persuasion model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use negotiation and mutual understanding as central goals; consider symmetric communication when choosing strategies rather than defaulting to persuasion/one-way approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public relations role as organizational ombudsman/in-house activist
rubrics_metrics.description: Portray public relations as a positive force that benefits publics at least as much as the employing organization and as 'in-house activists' who strive to make organizations responsible to the publics they affect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame PR counsel as interpreting the organization to publics and publics to the organization; avoid seeing PR merely as organizational apologetics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for management skills beyond technician skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations practitioners must develop management skills (not just technical writing/production skills) to participate in formulation and management of PR programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train practitioners in management, decision making, budgeting, evaluation, and systems thinking so they can rise above entry-level technician roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define what public relations is not
rubrics_metrics.description: Public relations is more than pleasant socializing, simple publicity, lobbying, advertising, or propaganda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify the distinct managerial and analytical functions of PR in education and practice to counter misconceptions (e.g., 'image-making' or 'flack' stereotypes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing objectives for PR materials
rubrics_metrics.description: PR writing should begin with clear writing objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before drafting a release or other material, define what effect or response you want (e.g., inform, persuade, motivate action) and measure success against those objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum objectivity in PR writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for maximum objectivity when writing public relations materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid unnecessary spin; present verifiable facts and context so media and publics can treat materials as credible information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source review and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct source review to verify facts and claims used in PR materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check primary sources, obtain permissions where necessary (copyright), and confirm factual accuracy to reduce legal and credibility risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider long-range implications and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate long-range implications and consistency of messages across programs and over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that releases align with broader organizational strategy and past/future communications to avoid contradictory or short-sighted messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Achieving maximum impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure writing and distribution to achieve maximum impact with intended publics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select salient angles, leads, and formats; time releases and choose channels to maximize attention and retention among target publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style considerations in PR writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt an appropriate matter of style for PR materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance objectivity with readability and conciseness; follow media conventions (AP style, lead-first structure) and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate your writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use evaluation to judge the effectiveness of PR writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply readership tests, message retention measures, and media pickup rates to refine future writing and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management considerations for press releases
rubrics_metrics.description: When preparing a press release, consider: Model of Public Relations; Objectives; Which Programs; Communication Behavior of Publics; Cost in Time and Money; Evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat a press release as part of a program—align it to the organization's PR model and objectives, assess target publics' communication behaviors, budget time/costs, and plan evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a news-release checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow a news-release checklist when producing a release (referenced as 'News-Release Checklist').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items typically include clear headline/lead, who/what/when/where/why, contact info, boilerplate, embargo instructions, distribution method, and media-friendly formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and embargo tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Time the release appropriately; use embargoes or hand delivery when necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide on embargoes to control timing of coverage; use hand delivery for sensitive materials or to specific reporters when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective submission and distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Be selective about whom to submit releases to and choose appropriate distribution channels (including PR wire services).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target media whose audiences match your publics; understand how wire services work and the information-retrieval link they provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal constraints and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect legal constraints: right to communicate; libel and slander; copyright; privacy; financial reporting requirements; regulation of advertising; consumer protection; rights of employees; lobbyist/foreign agent regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain permissions, avoid defamatory statements, adhere to disclosure rules (e.g., financial reporting/timely disclosure), and consult counsel when in doubt to 'live with the law.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation research methods for PR
rubrics_metrics.description: Use systematic evaluation methods: stages of evaluation; process evaluation; surveys; experiments; secondary data; qualitative analysis; time budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select measures (fact, evaluative, information, self-perception questions) and sample measures (communication, retention, acceptance, coorientation, attitudes, overt behavior) appropriate to objectives; determine who should evaluate and how to apply results to decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify publics and set objectives by public
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify organizational linkages to publics and use situational theory to classify publics; determine objectives for each public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze types of publics (active, passive, etc.), their information needs and involvement, then set tailored objectives and communication strategies for each group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting, scheduling, and decision-making for PR programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Define costs in PR budgets; use administrative and program budgets; apply network analysis (Gantt charts, PERT, CPM); and use decision tools (cost-benefit, expected-value analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate line items for PR activities, schedule tasks to meet critical paths, and use quantitative decision frameworks to select alternatives and allocate resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set PR objectives in terms of effects (MBO)
rubrics_metrics.description: Think in terms of effect when setting goals and objectives; make Management by Objectives (MBO) work for PR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define measurable effects (e.g., awareness, understanding, attitude change, behavior) and assign responsibility for decision-making and goal-setting, including two-way symmetric goal-setting where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand media relations dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize what helps and what hurts media relations; understand journalists' behavior and media publics; set media-relations objectives and evaluate via agenda-setting research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study journalist motives, access issues, and agenda-setting effects; tailor releases and pitches to journalistic processes and measure coverage and agenda influence as outcomes.
